request: Write an ADR from this thread.
input:
#backend channel, export of the thread

A: ok so we need to decide the job queue thing this week, the image resize jobs are still running inside the web request and people see timeouts
B: +1. I looked at BullMQ, it's nice, great dashboard. but it needs Redis and we don't run Redis today. that's a new thing to operate, back up and get paged for
A: we could use the managed Redis?
B: we could, about $90 a month for the small one, it's not the money, it's one more system in the on-call runbook. we are 4 people
C: what about SQS? no servers at all
B: SQS is fine in prod but local dev gets ugly, you need localstack or a real AWS account per dev, and our integration tests run offline in CI on purpose
C: fair. Kafka?
A: lol no. Kafka for 2 jobs a second is a joke, we'd spend a month on it
C: was half joking
D: what about pg-boss? it's a job queue on top of Postgres, we already run Postgres, jobs sit in a table, you get retries and delayed jobs and it uses SKIP LOCKED so workers don't fight
B: I like that there is no new infra. what's the ceiling though
D: I ran a test on staging friday. 350 jobs per second sustained with 4 workers before the queue table started to lag. we do about 2 per second now, peak maybe 15 during the nightly import
A: so we have like 20x headroom at peak. fine
B: downsides?
D: the jobs table bloats, completed jobs get archived and deleted but you need autovacuum tuned on that table or it grows. I'd add a weekly check. also it only has basic priorities, a number per job, no separate priority lanes. and if Postgres is down the queue is down, but then the app is down anyway
C: long jobs? the video transcode takes like 25 minutes
D: good point, pg-boss holds a job with an expiry, default 15 minutes. I would not put anything over 10 minutes in it. transcode should stay on the separate worker box like today, it has its own script
A: ok. so pg-boss for everything except jobs longer than 10 minutes, those stay on the transcode worker
B: and when do we look at this again? I don't want to be stuck on it at 300 jobs a second
D: if we pass 200 jobs per second sustained, or if we need priority lanes, we decide again. that's well before the 350 limit
A: agreed. also someone order pizza for thursday
C: on it
A: I'll write it up as an ADR. decision made today, 2026-10-14, all four agreed. D owns the migration of the resize job first, that's the one hurting users
B: and note that we said no to BullMQ because of the extra system, not because it's bad. if we ever run Redis for another reason that changes
A: yes good
